name: Caro-Kann Defense
blurb: A solid answer to 1.e4: Black prepares ...d5 with ...c6. It is like the French, but the c8 bishop gets out before the pawns close it in.

ideas.e4 c6: Prepares ...d5 with pawn support while keeping the c8 bishop's diagonal open, unlike the French.
ideas.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4: Trades off White's e4 pawn. After Nxe4, the bishop can come to f5 and attack the knight.
ideas.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5: The bishop develops outside the pawn chain before ...e6 and gains time by hitting the e4 knight.
ideas.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6: Steps back but stays on the same diagonal, still active.
ideas.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4: If White plays h5, the bishop now has h7 to retreat to.
ideas.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5: Against the Advance, the bishop comes out before ...e6 locks it in.
ideas.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 c3 e6: With the bishop already outside the chain, ...e6 no longer blocks it, and Black's position is solid.
ideas.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5: Recaptures with the c-pawn, keeping a pawn in the centre and a half-open c-file for Black's rook.
ideas.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6: Against the Panov, the knight develops and defends d5.
ideas.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6: Puts pressure on d4, which only White's queen defends now.
ideas.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4: Pins the f3 knight to the queen.
